title: Pair Seen
statement: Implement `solve(points)`. `points` is a list of `[x, y]` integer coordinates. Return how many points were new when seen in order. A repeated coordinate does not increase the count. `(1, 2)` and `(2, 1)` are different points.
constraints: Order of first appearance defines new
hints: Store tuples (x, y) in a set. Lists are not hashable.
Increment only when the tuple was absent, then add it.
The answer is the size of that set.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A coordinate is a pair, and a pair is hashable only as a tuple.

editorial: A coordinate is a pair, and a pair is hashable only as a tuple. Using a list as a set element throws. The count of successful inserts is the number of distinct points, which is also the final size of the set.
